jobs.name: Mixed correspondence folder (sample)

intake.valuable: From the correspondence, retain anything documenting decisions about the project's direction, its licensing and trademark position, its relationship with the University of Illinois, its handling of copyright questions, and its dealings with other digitisation efforts. Retain substantive exchanges with named individuals about specific texts or about how the work should be done. Retain a representative sample of the mailing list traffic rather than all of it, because the character of the list discussion is part of the record even though its bulk is not. The 1993 material should be retained in full regardless of content, on the grounds of age and the rarity of surviving campus mail from that period. From the loose files, retain the 1994 administrative correspondence and flag it as belonging to a different accession, and retain the [REDACTED] research databases and flag them the same way. Where a mailbox folder is substantially worth keeping, retain unidentified items filed alongside it and mark them as retained by association rather than on their own merits.
intake.exclude: Automated bounce and delivery failure notification. Out of office and auto-reply messages. Unsolicited commercial mail. Mailing list administrative traffic such as subscription confirmations and digest headers, as distinct from the list discussion itself. Duplicate copies of the same message appearing in more than one container. The 2017 saved web pages, social media captures and phone media, which appear to have been swept in by accident and have no evident relationship to any of the other material here.
intake.access: Closed pending review, and this is the accession where that matters most. The correspondence involves several hundred thousand messages from identifiable living correspondents who wrote to a project, not to an archive, and who had no expectation their mail would be published. Direct identifiers must be removed before any reading room access and quasi-identifiers before any open web release. The mixed-in material compounds the problem: the 1994 administrative correspondence names university officials in what may be personnel or governance matters, and the [REDACTED] fieldwork data may contain identifiable individuals in a research context with its own consent conditions that we know nothing about. Nothing from this accession should be published until its provenance is established and its several parts are separated.
intake.source: Withheld in the public build. The appraisal criteria above are the real ones and are what every ranking was scored against.

jobs.name: Scanning programme output (sample)

intake.valuable: PROVISIONAL, pending identification. Written as a general appraisal so the pipeline has something to work against, and to be replaced once the collection is identified. Retain images where content is legible and a subject is identifiable. Retain any image carrying text in frame that identifies what is being shown, such as a label, caption card, ruler, colour target, date board or accession number, because in an undocumented collection those are the only self-describing items and they anchor everything around them. Retain the first and last image of each contiguous run at minimum, since these usually carry a cover, title page or identifying label. Where a run of consecutive images is substantially worth keeping, retain the unidentifiable images within that run and mark them as retained by association, because a sequence of scans is a single object and thinning it destroys the thing it documents.
intake.exclude: Blank pages and scanner separator sheets, which appear here as very small files repeated identically many times. Exact duplicates within and across batches. Images with no recoverable content at any exposure. Calibration and test targets shot at the start of a session, unless they carry information about the capture itself that a preservation specialist would want.
intake.access: UNRESOLVED, pending identification. Treat as closed until the source collection is known. Two specific flags requested. First, mark any image whose content warrants a content note at publication, including offensive historical language or imagery appearing in the material being scanned; the flag is a description task and is never a reason to discard. Second, mark any image showing identifiable living people, private residences, or documents containing personal information, so that a person decides on release rather than the machine.
intake.source: Withheld in the public build. The appraisal criteria above are the real ones and are what every ranking was scored against.

jobs.name: Faculty office computer (sample)

intake.valuable: Retain anything that documents how the research was done rather than only its published result. Specifically: drafts carrying handwritten or tracked revisions, referee reports and the correspondence that accompanies them, and the [REDACTED] material including the written comments from external participants, which record a professional discussion that exists nowhere else. Retain the Consulting folder in full, because industrial consulting is chronically under-documented in academic collections and the client relationship is itself part of the record. Retain the [REDACTED] mailboxes as mailboxes, not as loose messages, because the folder a message was filed in carries the creator's own judgement about what it related to. Retain figures and data files even where they appear orphaned, since a specialist may be able to reunite them with the paper they belong to. Where a folder is substantially made up of material worth keeping, retain unidentified files sitting alongside it rather than removing them, but mark them as retained by association so a reviewer can see the difference between a file we understand and a file we kept because of its neighbours.
intake.exclude: Personal genealogy and family biography, which are unrelated to the professional record and should be offered back rather than accessioned. Published papers by other authors collected as reference copies, which the library already holds and which carry no annotation making this copy distinctive. Duplicate exposures and repeated downloads of the same document. Dropbox conflicted copies where an identical resolved version is present. Application working files from the [REDACTED] installation, including logs, nicknames and link history, which record software behaviour rather than the creator's activity.
intake.access: Open by default. Three exceptions to flag rather than to withhold automatically. Referee reports and reviews may name identifiable people and make critical judgements about their work, and some of those people are living; route these to the supervising archivist. Consulting material may carry contractual confidentiality obligations that outlived the engagement, so the [REDACTED] folder needs a check against any surviving agreement before publication. The mailboxes contain ordinary personal correspondence mixed with professional exchanges and will need redaction review before any release. No student records are expected in this accession, but flag anything resembling one.
intake.source: Withheld in the public build. The appraisal criteria above are the real ones and are what every ranking was scored against.

jobs.name: Departmental transfer (queued)

intake.valuable: PROVISIONAL. Retain material documenting how the work was done rather than only its results: drafts with revisions, correspondence with collaborators and sponsors, and grant administration records. Retain teaching materials that show the development of a course rather than a single final syllabus.
intake.exclude: Duplicate copies. Published papers by other authors held as reference copies. Software installers and application working files.
intake.access: Closed pending review. Flag anything resembling a student record, and any correspondence that names identifiable living people in an evaluative context.
